ios.desc:
Treeline puts wilderness on the map. Explore and plan hikes, with beautiful topo maps, satellite imagery, and detailed information about trails, amenities, and points of interest, no connection required. While you have service, 20 more live data layers give you up-to-the-minute info on weather, active fires, and more.

Features:
- A beautiful, detailed, fully custom topo basemap inspired by NPS maps.
- 20+ layers, including public land boundaries, NPS maps, USFS and BLM roads, live weather, cell coverage, aircraft, historical mines and minerals, and bedrock geology.
- Combine and overlap layers however you want. Save presets to switch between different setups quickly.
- Record routes. Organize your saved routes and places, share them with friends, and customize them on the map.
- Navigate by foot and car. Build custom routes using any combination of modes, and save them to reference (or navigate) later. Preview elevation profiles in detail.
- Import and export KML, GPX, and GeoJSON.
- See an exact forecast for any point on the map.
- Generate viewsheds so you know what you'll be able to see from a peak or a campsite.
- Discover trailheads, campsites, water sources, landmarks, caves, and more. When you're back in town for a resupply, see grocery stores and gas stations.
- Download maps offline on demand.
- ...And lots and lots and lots of other cool stuff!

Map coverage is presently limited to North America.

EULA: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/

show_hn.title: Show HN: Treeline – beautiful, powerful wilderness topo maps for iOS

quotes.text:
Hey HN!

I really love hiking, camping, and backpacking, and I try to get out into the middle of nowhere as much as I possibly can. I could never leave on a trip without a good topo map downloaded.

Over the last couple years, though, I've gotten pretty fed up with the existing options when it comes to offline maps. Gaia is expensive and buggy; CalTopo is ugly, dated, and battery-sucking (the map is an embedded webview); AllTrails isn't fully-featured enough for serious backcountry trips; OsmAnd is ugly and lacks some basic features for the backcountry. Several major players have been purchased by private equity and are just getting worse.

I hate to be this critical of tools that have obviously had a lot of love and care put into them, but they haven't kept up with the times, and I really think the outdoor recreation community deserves better.

So Treeline is my attempt to build that. It has all the major features of Gaia et al. It has a fully custom basemap (with style inspiration from NPS and USFS maps - I think it's quite pretty!), offline downloads, POIs (campsites, water, etc.), detailed point info, search, navigation, route recording, saved features, 20+ useful layers, and a lot more.

You can download maps for offline use and access all the overlays for $18/year flat. That price is lower than any comparable app, and it will stay fixed through at least 2027.
